reliability.title: How reliable is this?
reliability.p1: Every instruction here is confirmed by at least two independent sources: different authors, not copies of each other. Where sources disagree or say nothing, the app says so instead of filling the gap.
reliability.p2: The animation is an illustration. The timing is slow motion, and stick travel is drawn on one scale (little, half, strong, full). These are not measured values.
reliability.p3: Models differ. Set-up, power, wind and propeller direction change what is needed, so the values are guideline values. Check them in a simulator or with an experienced pilot.
reliability.legendConfirmed: Confirmed: at least two independent sources agree.
reliability.legendDisputed: Sources disagree: the sources contradict each other.
reliability.legendGap: No confirmed instruction: the sources say nothing, or only one source does.
reliability.legendIllustration: Illustration: shown in the animation, but not confirmed by the sources.

footer.colours: Top side teal with the canopy, underside coral. The control surfaces move as the sticks move. A control surface with deflection glows yellow-orange (stronger = more deflection) and fades for about a second, also in the control schematic (▲ = trailing edge up, ▼ = down). Yellow waves at the sticks are constant small corrections.

knife-edge.name: Knife edge
knife-edge.idea: The model flies straight on its side. The rudder holds it there.

instructions.across: Fly the pass across your front, left to right or right to left.
instructions.height: For the first attempts, start with plenty of height.
instructions.throttle: Fly with medium to high throttle.

instructions.quarter-roll: Roll with the aileron from level flight until the wings are about vertical (a quarter turn).
instructions.rudder-opposite: From upright flight, add rudder opposite to the roll: roll right, rudder left; roll left, rudder right.
instructions.two-steps: While learning, practise the quarter roll first without rudder, and add the rudder once the bank is set.

instructions.rudder-holds: The rudder carries the model on its side. Without it, the model does not stay there.
instructions.rudder-cue: Cue: canopy toward you, rudder stick toward the tail; belly toward you, rudder stick toward the nose.
instructions.rudder-amount: How much rudder you need depends on the model and its speed. Faster flight needs less.
instructions.tuck: Rudder makes the nose tuck. Which way depends on the model: toward the landing gear or toward the canopy.
instructions.tuck-elevator: Correct the tuck with the elevator. If the nose tucks toward the landing gear, give a little up elevator.
instructions.roll-aileron: If the model starts to roll, correct with a little aileron. The direction depends on the model.
instructions.throttle-height: The throttle adds or removes height: if the model sinks, add throttle.

notes.altitude: Sources disagree on what holds the height: some say the rudder does, others say the rudder only sets the nose angle and the throttle holds the height.
notes.duration: How long to hold the knife edge: the sources give no confirmed value.

instructions.quarter-back: Roll a quarter turn back with the aileron to upright, and take the rudder and elevator inputs off.

illustration.sides: Which side of the model faces you, and the exact stick travel and timing, are an illustration. The sources give the rules above, not these values.

elevator.name: Elevator
elevator.idea: The model sinks on a steep to nearly vertical line with the elevator pulled fully, nose high and stalled.

instructions.slow-to-stall: Slow the model down to the stall: cut or reduce the throttle and pull up elevator.
instructions.progressive: Pull the elevator smoothly, not abruptly.

instructions.full-up: Hold the elevator pulled fully, or almost fully.
instructions.steep-descent: The model sinks on a steep to nearly vertical line.
instructions.throttle-little: Add a little throttle to keep the nose up. Changing the throttle moves the nose up or down.
instructions.rudder-heading: The rudder corrects the heading, left and right.
instructions.aileron-small: Catch a rocking wing with small, brief aileron inputs.

notes.throttle: Throttle in the hold: most sources add a little throttle, one source says idle.
notes.levelling: What levels the wings: some sources say mainly the rudder, others say the ailerons.

instructions.release: To fly out, release the up elevator and add throttle.
instructions.into-harrier: You can also exit into a harrier instead of flying out.

notes.min-height: How low you may go before the exit: the sources give no confirmed value.

harrier.name: Harrier
harrier.idea: Slow flight with the nose about 45° up. The elevator sets the nose attitude, the throttle holds the height.

instructions.rates: Practise with high control rates switched on.

instructions.reduce-and-pull: Reduce the throttle while you feed in up elevator gradually.
instructions.from-elevator: Coming from an elevator: add throttle until the sinking stops and the model moves forward.

instructions.elevator-attitude: The elevator holds the nose attitude. The throttle decides whether the model holds its height.
instructions.more-thrust: The harrier needs clearly more thrust than ordinary slow flight.
instructions.throttle-pumps: Use the throttle actively in short pumps instead of setting it once.
instructions.rudder-rolls: Rudder also rolls the model the same way: rudder left rolls it left.
instructions.torque-rudder: With a standard propeller rotation, hold some right rudder against the propeller torque.

notes.aileron: Aileron in the harrier: one manufacturer manual says to avoid it because it may snap the model. Other sources use small aileron inputs to keep the wings level.

instructions.throttle-up: Raise the throttle toward full and lower the nose with the elevator so the model regains speed.
instructions.emergency: If the figure goes wrong, go to full throttle.

hover.name: Hover
hover.idea: The model hangs vertically on its propeller. The throttle holds the height.

instructions.simulator: Practise on a flight simulator first.
instructions.safe-height: Practise at a safe height and hold the hover only briefly at first.

notes.start-height: Starting height: the sources give very different values, so none is shown.

instructions.from-harrier: Enter from a harrier: keep adding up elevator until the model is vertical.

notes.entry-orientation: Which way you fly at entry and which side of the model faces you: the sources do not say.

instructions.throttle-height: The throttle controls the height: more power climbs, less power sinks.
instructions.throttle-bursts: After each correction a short burst of throttle is needed. Holding high throttle makes the model climb out of the hover.
instructions.aileron-torque: The propeller torque tries to turn the model about its long axis. Aileron against the torque stops it. In the models these sources describe, that is right aileron.
instructions.rudder-elevator: Rudder and elevator keep the model vertical: rudder for left and right, elevator for forward and back.
instructions.small-early: Corrections should be small, short and early, not held.
instructions.belly-in-rudder: With the belly toward you, push the rudder stick toward the wing that is dropping.

notes.elevator-direction: Which way to move the elevator when the nose tilts toward or away from you: the sources do not say.
notes.exit: How to exit the hover: the sources give no confirmed instruction.

illustration.orientation: The animation shows the model entering by flying away and pulling up, with the canopy toward you. The sources do not confirm this. It is an illustration, as are stick travel and timing.

torque-roll.name: Torque roll
torque-roll.idea: A hover in which the model also turns about its long axis, driven by the propeller torque.

instructions.calm-air: Practise in calm air. Wind makes it much harder.
instructions.simulator: Practise on a flight simulator first.

instructions.pull-vertical: Pull the model to a fully vertical hover. The propeller carries it.
instructions.let-it-turn: Do not counter the torque: in a clean hover the model starts to rotate by itself.

instructions.torque-turns: The propeller torque makes the model rotate about its long axis.
instructions.turns-left: The torque turns the model to the left.
instructions.rudder-elevator: Rudder and elevator keep the long axis of the model vertical.
instructions.throttle-steps: Adjust the throttle in small steps so the model neither climbs nor sinks.
instructions.large-throws: Large control surfaces and large throws help.

notes.belly-in: The controls may seem reversed while the belly faces you. Only one source describes this, so it is not given as an instruction.

instructions.aileron-stops: Aileron against the torque (right aileron) slows or stops the rotation.

notes.exit: How to end the torque roll and leave the hover: the sources give no confirmed instruction.

illustration.orientation: The animation shows a hover with the canopy toward you. The sources do not say which side faces you. It is an illustration, as are stick travel and timing.
illustration.viewpoint: The sources say the torque turns the model to the left, but not from which viewpoint. The animation shows it rolling to the left as seen from behind the model.

rolling-harrier.name: Rolling harrier
rolling-harrier.idea: A harrier in which the model also rolls continuously about its long axis while holding its height.

instructions.harrier-first: Learn the plain harrier first, upright and inverted.
instructions.slow-rolls: Practise slow rolls with rudder and elevator support before you try this.
instructions.high-rates: Set large control travel on rudder and elevator and reduced exponential, so inputs respond without delay.
instructions.advanced: This is an advanced figure that needs a lot of practice.

entry.title: Nose up and start the roll

instructions.from-harrier: Start from an established nose-high harrier. Ease the elevator, then command full aileron and begin to roll.
instructions.attitude: The sources give a nose-up attitude of roughly 35° to 60°.

instructions.aileron-full: Hold full aileron in one direction for the whole roll and release it only at the exit.
instructions.alternate: Rudder and elevator come in one after the other during each roll while the aileron stays fixed. The timing is the hard part.
instructions.rudder-knife: The rudder works hardest when the model is on its side. Near upright and near inverted, the elevator does the work.
instructions.elevator-sequence: Toward inverted, give down elevator. Coming back round to upright, change to up elevator.
instructions.throttle-hold: Use the throttle to hold height and keep the nose up: more power raises the nose, less lets it drop.
instructions.timing-drift: The timing of the rudder and elevator inputs decides which way the model drifts sideways.
instructions.slow-roll: If the roll gets slower, that is a sign of too little power: add throttle.

notes.throttle-start: Throttle at the start of the roll: one source adds a few clicks, one uses medium-to-low throttle, one cuts the power. There is no agreed rule.
notes.rudder-needed: Is the rudder needed? Most sources use it. Some say rolling with elevator only works but looks poor, and one says it is not workable.
notes.rudder-direction: Which way the rudder goes relative to the roll direction, and how far: the sources do not say.

instructions.exit-inputs: Add power, release the aileron and reduce the elevator to return to normal forward flight.

illustration.direction: The animation rolls the model to the left, with the rudder toward the top of the model. The sources do not give the roll direction or the rudder direction. Roll speed, stick travel and throttle are illustrations too.

flat-spin.name: Flat spin
flat-spin.idea: The model spins flat about the vertical axis, with power, while staying roughly level.

instructions.height: Start high. The exit needs more height than a conventional spin, because airspeed has to be rebuilt from a flat attitude.
instructions.models-differ: Not every model flat spins, and models differ widely in how well they enter and recover.
instructions.cg: A rearward centre of gravity helps the model to flat spin.
instructions.throws: Use large control throws on all controls.
instructions.simulator: Practise on a flight simulator first. The real model may behave differently.

instructions.from-spin: Start from an ordinary spin: slow the model, stall it, begin the spin, and only then flatten it.
instructions.bleed-speed: Bleed off the speed: reduce the throttle toward idle and raise the nose until the model stalls.
instructions.full-inputs: At entry the elevator is full up and the rudder is full toward the spin direction.

notes.aileron-entry: Aileron at entry: some sources say the same direction as the rudder, one says the opposite direction, one says it depends on the model.

instructions.hold-inputs: Once the spin is established, hold elevator and rudder at their large deflections while you tune the rest.
instructions.aileron-ease: To flatten the spin, bring the aileron slowly toward neutral or toward the opposite side, never abruptly.
instructions.add-throttle: Add some throttle to help flatten the spin and to keep the model from falling fast.
instructions.tail-authority: A little throttle gives the rudder and elevator more authority at the tail.

instructions.throttle-height: With throttle the model can hold its height or even climb. Without throttle it falls slowly.

notes.spin-rate: How to control the spin rate and how long to hold the spin: the sources give no confirmed instruction.

instructions.release: Centre or release the sticks. Some models then stop rotating on their own.
instructions.opposite-rudder: If it keeps rotating, give rudder opposite to the rotation.
instructions.more-turns: Releasing the sticks does not always stop it at once. Several more turns are possible.

notes.exit-throttle: Throttle during the exit: one source says idle until airspeed builds, two forum posters say power is what makes the exit possible.
notes.recoverable: Can a flat spin be exited at all? One wiki says a flat spin means losing the model. Other sources say the exit is routine with a suitable model and correct inputs.

illustration.illustration: The animation shows no aileron, because the sources disagree on its direction and amount. The spin direction (to the left), the throttle level and the stick travel are illustrations.
